themeRoles.note: Role tokens are CSS custom properties on :root in tools/team-office/public/style.css. Dark is the stylesheet default; light applies under prefers-color-scheme: light unless data-theme="dark", or when data-theme="light".

fonts.bundledUnusedNote: Font files and licences remain in fonts/; no @font-face rule loads them.

shadows.name: lift (dark)
shadows.purpose: A sheet on the desk at night: lit top edge, deep soft drop. Panels, banners/setup/welcome, ask-banner, in-grid chat, launch card.

shadows.name: lift-high (dark)
shadows.purpose: A sheet held above the desk at night: floating chat and dialogs.

shadows.name: lift (light)
shadows.purpose: A sheet on the desk by day: 1px contact line, soft offset drop. Same surfaces as dark --lift.

shadows.name: lift-high (light)
shadows.purpose: A sheet held up by day: floating chat and dialogs.

shadows.name: stamp-fall (transient)
shadows.purpose: Only inside the stamp-land keyframes: the falling stamp's shadow shrinks as it nears the paper.

extensions.shadowsNote: Shadows only via --lift / --lift-high (role tokens, defined per theme) and the falling stamp. No glows, glass, backdrop blur or gradient fills. The dialog scrim rgb(0 0 0 / .6) is the only overlay. Lifting never removes the 1.5px rule.

motion.name: ease-out (--out)
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out: stamp press-and-settle, wheel roll, page-in, dialog rise, progress fill, press, scrim fade.

motion.name: ease-in-fall
motion.purpose: A stamp falling toward the page (speeds up).

motion.name: ease-in-lift-away
motion.purpose: The old view lifting away in the page turn.

motion.name: stamp-land
motion.value: stamp-land .7s both; 0% translateY(var(--fall-y,-18px)) scale(var(--fall-s,1.4)) rotateX(34deg) rotate(-8deg), opacity 0, shadow 0 20px 16px -8px (ease-in) → 22% opacity 1 → 52% translateY(0) scale(.92) rotate(-2deg), contact shadow (ease-out) → 56% ink on (--stamp-ink/--stamp-on) → 100% rest; perspective 520px on .stepper/.signoff
motion.purpose: The focal moment: a station's stamp falls, presses and leaves its ink when its step completes while you watch.

motion.name: stamp-land-stepper
motion.purpose: Stepper station that just completed (.stepper li.stamped .dot).

motion.name: stamp-land-signoff
motion.purpose: A newly finished project's sign-off strip (.signoff.landing .stamp); portfolio.js compares status with the previous refresh.

motion.name: wheel-roll
motion.value: transform .9s var(--out); drum rotateX(var(--d) * 36deg), faces rotateX(i * -36deg) translateZ(1.08em), perspective 7em
motion.purpose: Numbering machine in the commission number box; --d counts cumulative turns so wheels only roll forward (progress.js roll()).

motion.name: page-in
motion.value: page-in .6s var(--out) both; from perspective(1400px) rotateX(-72deg), opacity 0; transform-origin 50% 0
motion.purpose: A new commission entry turns into the book, hinged at its top rule (.pf-card.turning).

motion.name: page-away
motion.value: ::view-transition-old(root) page-away .55s cubic-bezier(.55, 0, .75, .35) both; to perspective(2600px) rotateY(-90deg); transform-origin 0 50%; z-index 1; new view not animated
motion.purpose: Simple ⇄ Behind the scenes on a user click only (ui.js setView({turn})); never under reduced motion or without View Transition support.

motion.name: sheet-up
motion.value: sheet-up .3s var(--out) both; from perspective(1200px) translateY(14px) rotateX(6deg)
motion.purpose: A dialog rises into your hands.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Background/colour transitions on buttons, chips, tabs, switches; 1px press on :active.

motion.name: two-step-blink
motion.purpose: Typing caret and launch progress; stepped, never a smooth pulse.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; transition: none (all); view transitions off; stamps ink-in .3s linear, sign-off stagger 100ms
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: nothing moves, wheels jump, stamps fade their ink in.

narrative.overview:
The studio is a workshop's commission book. Every idea is a numbered commission, and the crew signs it off station by station with a stamp. The pages are sheets of sage and black paper divided by crisp 1.5px rules, with square corners. Depth comes only from the book as a physical object: a sheet lifts off the desk with a soft, offset shadow, a stamp falls and presses its ink into the page, a numbering machine's wheels roll, and pages turn on their hinge. There are no glows, no glass and no gradient fills. The system rejects the category default of a glowing dark dashboard with glass cards.

The book has two moods that follow the computer's setting, and Settings can force either one (`data-theme="light" | "dark"` on the root). In the light theme the book lies open on the bench: sage ground, pale sage paper, black ink, a black cover band. In the dark theme the book is read at night: black ground, sage ink, a sage cover band. Each theme mirrors the other; only where ground and ink sit changes. Each theme also has its own light on the paper (a lit top edge at night, a contact line by day), carried by the same two lift tokens. One red exists, and it means "error" or "blocked". It is never decoration.

Two worlds share the screen on purpose. The pixel-art office and the teammates keep their own colours: name tags, portrait frames, signer squares, log dots and Maya's face on the chat button. The two-tone system frames them and never recolours them. Archivo, a single variable font bundled for offline use, carries every voice. Its condensed, uppercase, spaced cut is the book's hand for labels, numbers and stamps. Its normal width is for reading.
keyCharacteristics: Two colours (sage `#9cb29e`, black `#000000`) with tints and shades, plus one red reserved for errors and blocked work.
Light and dark themes are exact inversions, chosen by the OS and overridable in Settings.
1.5px black (or sage) rules and 0px corners. Sheets sit on the page with a soft, offset paper shadow (`--lift`, `--lift-high`), never a glow.
Status is shown as a stamp in a fixed box: filled, sage, hollow, dashed, or red and struck through.
Motion comes only from the physical book: a stamp falls and presses, number wheels roll, pages turn, dialogs rise into your hands. Under reduced motion nothing moves and stamps fade their ink in.
The Simple view landing page fits a desktop window with no page scroll. Long content scrolls inside its own panel.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Every chrome surface, rule and text is either sage, black, or a tint or shade of sage. If a new colour is needed, use a sage tint first.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red means an error or blocked work, and nothing else. It is never used for emphasis, a brand accent or decoration.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Each theme is the other with ground and ink swapped. Build every component against the role tokens (`--page`, `--paper`, `--ink`, `--accent`, `--on-accent`, `--band`, `--on-band`, `--lift`, `--lift-high`), never against a theme's literal value, so the inversion stays automatic.

rules.name: The Crew Keeps Its Colours Rule
rules.body: Teammate identity colours (name-tag squares, portrait frames, signer marks, log dots), the pixel office scenery and the pixel-art face on Maya's chat button sit outside the two-tone system. Never recolour them to sage or black, and never borrow them for chrome.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: Condensed uppercase is for things the book prints or stamps: labels, numbers and statuses. Anything you read as a sentence uses normal width and sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Times, logs, tables, the progress figure and every commission number use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Fits-The-Window Rule
rules.body: At ≥1101×600, the Simple view landing page never scrolls the page. The body is a 100dvh column. The header and banners take their natural height, and the grid takes the rest, with rows split 1.12fr / 1fr. Every panel is `min-height: 0`. Long content (old messages, many commissions, the start card's overflow) scrolls inside its own box. A visible thin scrollbar track marks the commission book as having more entries. The office screen sizes itself to `min(100cqw - 200px, (100cqh - 6px) × 16/9)`, with who's who beside it.

rules.name: The Paper Lift Rule
rules.body: A sheet's shadow is always `--lift` or `--lift-high`: offset downward, blurred, and the colour of the room, never the colour of the ink. Nothing else casts a shadow except a stamp while it is falling. No glows, no coloured or spread halos, no blur behind glass, no gradient fills.

rules.name: The Ruled And Lifted Rule
rules.body: Lifting a sheet never replaces its rule. Every lifted surface keeps its 1.5px ink border and square corners, and emphasis inside it is still a 3px rule, not a higher lift.

rules.name: The Physical Book Rule
rules.body: Every authored movement is something a real book, stamp or numbering machine does: a stamp falls and presses, a wheel rolls, a page turns on its hinge, a sheet is lifted into your hands. The ease-out is exponential (`--out`: `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`); things that fall or lift away speed up instead (ease-in). Nothing bounces, pulses, glows or floats.

rules.name: The Stamp Lands Rule
rules.body: The focal moment is a station's stamp landing, in .7s. The stamp starts above the page, tilted back (`rotateX(34deg) rotate(-8deg)`), enlarged and invisible, with a large soft shadow beneath it. It falls into view on an ease-in (`cubic-bezier(.55, 0, 1, .45)`), fully visible by 22%. At 52% it presses (`scale(.92)`, shadow shrunk to a contact line), then rises back to rest on the exponential ease-out; its ink (`--stamp-ink` / `--stamp-on`, the done colours) is on the page from 56%. The stepper and the sign-off strip set a 520px perspective. In the stepper, a station whose step completes while you watch falls from 18px above at 1.4×. When a project finishes while you watch, its sign-off strip's four stamps land one by one, falling from 9px at 1.18×, 150ms apart after a 200ms wait. The commission book compares each project's status with the previous refresh to decide this, so stamps land only for what just happened.

rules.name: The Page Turn Rule
rules.body: A new commission entry turns in like a page hinged at its top rule (from `rotateX(-72deg)` on a 1400px perspective, transparent, over .6s on the ease-out). Switching between Simple and Behind the scenes by clicking the switch turns the page: the old view, drawn above the new one, lifts away from its left edge to `rotateY(-90deg)` on a 2600px perspective over .55s on an ease-in (`cubic-bezier(.55, 0, .75, .35)`), uncovering the new view beneath. It is a same-document View Transition and runs only on a user's click, only where the browser supports it.

rules.name: The Still Book Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every animation and transition is removed and no view transition runs. The wheels jump straight to the number. The only thing that changes over time is a stamp's ink: it fades in over .3s, linear, with a finished project's four stamps 100ms apart.

dos: **Do** build every surface from the role tokens (`--page`, `--paper`, `--paper-2`, `--inset`, `--ink`, `--accent`/`--on-accent`, `--band`/`--on-band`, `--lift`/`--lift-high`) so both themes come for free.
**Do** separate surfaces with the 1.5px `--rule` and keep every chrome corner at 0px.
**Do** lift a sheet only with `--lift` (lying on the page) or `--lift-high` (floating chat, dialogs): a downward offset with a soft blur, plus the theme's lit edge or contact line.
**Do** express status only through the stamp grammar: filled done, sage in progress, hollow waiting, dashed pending, red and struck blocked.
**Do** set labels, stamps and numbers in condensed (62–72%) uppercase Archivo at 0.07em, with tabular figures for numbers.
**Do** keep text pairs at ≥4.5:1 (the floor is Muted Ink on sage, 4.80:1) and focus outlines at 3px.
**Do** keep the desktop Simple view (≥1101×600) free of page scroll. New content scrolls inside its panel, and container queries shed secondary lines before anything scrolls.
**Do** keep teammates' identity colours, the pixel office's own palette and Maya's pixel face untouched inside the two-tone frame.

**Do** take every movement from the physical-book set (stamp fall and press, wheel roll, page turn, sheet rise) and land it on the exponential ease-out; animate only what just happened while the person watched.
**Do** keep reduced motion still: no movement, no view transition, wheels jump, and stamps fade their ink in over .3s.
donts: **Don't** cast a shadow outside the two lift tokens and the falling stamp, and never a hard offset block shadow. The day theme's 1px contact line belongs to `--lift`; it is not a device of its own.

**Don't** add glows, glass, backdrop blur or decorative gradient fills. A hard-stop gradient used as a progress rule, the overflow fade on a sideways-scrolling row and the number wheels' window mask are the only gradients, and all are functional.
**Don't** use red for anything but errors and blocked work.
**Don't** introduce a third hue into the chrome. Use a sage tint or shade instead.
**Don't** round corners or use round status dots in the chrome. The system's dot is a square.
**Don't** add motion outside the physical-book set: no bounce, pulse, float, parallax, hover lift or looping ambient movement. State changes stay short colour transitions.
**Don't** use the pixel fonts left in the fonts folder (Press Start 2P, VT323) for the interface. Archivo is the only interface face.
